The evidence points to missing data in the source feed, not a pipeline bug.

- Raw merchant_id has 378 NULLs, and batch 14 has 378 rows.
- The batch 14 sample rows all show merchant_id as None, so batch 14 appears to be entirely NULL.
- 363 of those NULLs are POSTED, which matches the silver alert. The other 15 are presumably REVERSED.
- The gold_mcc_daily gap is 4630 − 4267 = 363, so the inner join drops exactly those NULL-merchant rows.

The merchant for these transactions cannot be derived from anything in the data. The customer, amount and timestamp do not identify a merchant, and guessing would produce wrong mcc aggregates. The upstream source has to re-deliver batch 14 with merchant_id populated.

Changing the pipeline would not fix this. Mapping the NULLs to an "unknown" mcc would change the meaning of the tables and hide the missing data. Filtering out batch 14 would drop real transactions from the counts and spend totals. Escalating is the right call.
